introduction: Help a busy mother prepare supper and learn the tanner’s three separate skin trades. The journal explains exact materials and accepted exchanges alongside Kimordril’s shared town services.
orientation: The busy dwarven mother asks for a potato, a carrot and a new cutting knife together. Ask about help or vegetables to hear the request. All three exact items must be available for the accepted errand.

Two potatoes look identical, but the errand requires the kind stored in the fungi crate above Dorfgon’s shop. The other potato does not fit. The journal checks the exact errand item rather than its displayed name.

Dorfgon’s shop normally supplies the potato, carrot and cutting knife, but purchases are currently unavailable while accounting is active. The journal cannot promise a new shop purchase. Existing or supplied materials can fit the request without proving your own purchase.

Recover the errand potato from the storage crate when available, follow ordinary container rules, and carry the materials loose. Readiness describes what you have now; it does not record finding or buying anything.

The mother who accepts the complete errand departs. Two mother instances can reset in separate homes, and their availability is shared. A new daily entry does not immediately bring back a mother or restock the world.

The dirty dwarf in the Tanners Guild pays separately for goatskin, black boarskin and brown boarskin. Some grazing animals carry prepared skins as stock; not every animal instance carries one. These trades do not require carving a corpse or a journal record of your own kill.

Give each exact skin to the tanner for its own accepted trade. Brown and black boarskins are different items even though they share targeting words. Goat meat, duplicate skins and an animal encounter do not replace another kind.

Hidden panels, gates, the cell key, the general’s defenders and the town’s bank, inn, stables, forge, postal center and bartender provide separate routes and services. Visiting them or receiving their equipment does not complete these four exchanges.

contacts.name: a busy dwarven mother
contacts.description: Needs a potato, a carrot and a cutting knife together for the family supper. The mother you help leaves after accepting the complete errand.

contacts.name: a dirty dwarf
contacts.description: Pays separately for goatskin, black boarskin and brown boarskin. Bring each exact kind; completing one trade does not complete the others.

contacts.name: Dorfgon
contacts.description: Dorfgon supplies the errand materials, but his shop purchases are currently unavailable while accounting is active. Existing or supplied items can still fit the request.

contacts.name: a goat
contacts.description: Some goats in the grazing fields carry prepared goatskin. Not every animal instance carries it; the accepted skin trade is separate from a personal hunt.

contacts.name: an angry boar
contacts.description: Some angry boars carry prepared black boarskin. Bring the black skin to the tanner; an animal encounter or brown skin does not replace it.

contacts.name: a tame boar
contacts.description: Some tame boars carry prepared brown boarskin. Bring the brown skin to the tanner; an animal encounter or black skin does not replace it.

contacts.name: a brutish bartender
contacts.description: The Mother Lode bartender offers separate world quests. Those assignments, fees and rewards are distinct from these four local exchanges.

contacts.name: General Kimordril
contacts.description: The general patrols the stronghold and can call elite guards during combat. Fighting or meeting him does not complete the local errands.

contacts.name: the High Priestess
contacts.description: The High Priestess guides visitors toward the bank for coin conversion. Her service and temple lore are separate from the accepted local requests.

contacts.name: Ratroper
contacts.description: Ratroper is the town’s banker. Banking and locker services are separate from an accepted supper or skin exchange.

contacts.name: a dwarven postal clerk
contacts.description: The postal-center clerk provides town context. Visiting the postal center does not complete a delivery story.

contacts.name: The Justice Clerk
contacts.description: The House of Justice clerk provides town context. Crime, imprisonment and prison access are separate from the four local requests.

contacts.name: Gildak
contacts.description: Gildak works at the armory. Equipment and craft services do not stand in for accepted local errand receipts.

contacts.name: the beastmaster
contacts.description: The beastmaster tends the stables. Mounting, training and animal care remain separate from a skin exchange.

stories.title: Help prepare the family supper
